chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from Abu Al-Maghra, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
He said: If a man dies and leaves behind his paternal aunt and his maternal aunt, then for the paternal aunt are two-thirds, and for the maternal aunt is one-third.
ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a paternal aunt versus a maternal aunt in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the distribution of the estate between the paternal aunt (ammah) and maternal aunt (khalah) when they are the sole heirs, assigning two-thirds to the paternal aunt and one-third to the maternal aunt. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the strength of the paternal lineage in inheritance shares, distinguishing it from other schools of thought that may treat them equally or prioritize the maternal line differently. The hadith serves as a foundational text for understanding the specific allocation of fixed shares (fara'id) among collateral relatives in the absence of closer heirs.
